_comment: AgentalSec Linux configuration. Copy to config.json and edit, or simply
delete config.json and let main.py create it from this file on first run.
SHAPE ONLY -- no secrets. API keys live in .env:
AGENTAL_API_KEY           the model provider key
AGENTAL_APP_API_KEY       AgentalSec's REST key, 64 hex chars
AGENTAL_ROUTER_COMMUNITY  SNMP read community, if router_monitor is on
AGENTAL_SSH_KEY_PATH      private key for linux_monitor's SSH path
EVERY BLOCK IN THE RUNNING FILE IS REPRESENTED HERE, checked against
main.py's own readers rather than against a template that drifted. It was
missing the seven blocks below that carry the agentic half of the app,
which meant a fresh install booted with no incident watcher, no action
executor and no duty loop, and the dashboard reported them as missing
rather than as switched off by the operator's choice.
The defaults here are the code's own defaults, so deleting this file and
letting main.py write a fresh config.json lands in the same place.
Any provider works. Fill in the three values for yours.
model: the id your provider uses for the model you want.
api_url: the provider's chat endpoint. Either an OpenAI-style
.../v1/chat/completions URL or an Anthropic-style .../v1/messages URL.
api_style: auto, openai or anthropic. Auto reads it from api_url.
The key goes in .env as AGENTAL_API_KEY, never here.
max_output_tokens: the answer budget, reasoning comes out of it.
context_budget: our cap on how much gets sent per turn.
Threat map. Needs maxminddb (pip install -r requirements.txt) and the
database itself. Without either, the geoip sensor is SKIPPED at boot
with the reason in the log, and the map says why it is empty.
Run scripts/fetch_geoip.py to download the database (CC-BY 4.0).
asn_db_path is optional: network owner names on the map and network
baselines. Download it with scripts/fetch_geoip.py --asn.
Dashboard binding. 127.0.0.1 for local-only, 0.0.0.0 for LAN access.
Add the name you browse to under allowed_hosts when binding beyond
loopback, or the Host header check answers 403.
auto_open_browser: opens a browser when the listener is up.
Enable/disable individual sensors.
Some need root or CAP_NET_RAW; see core/privilege_linux.py and the
privilege report main.py prints before any module loads.
PS-13 option (c), 2026-09-25. The TCP pass has two methods now and
the payload names the one that ran (tcp_method on every scan).
"auto"    SYN where a raw socket opens (CAP_NET_RAW or root), the
connect test where it does not. An absent key means this,
so a config written before the key existed is unchanged.
"syn"     SYN only. With no raw socket the TCP pass REFUSES by name
rather than quietly substituting a connect test -- the
substitution is exactly the defect PS-13 is about.
"connect" the connect test only, even when a raw socket is
available.
Read from port_scan.tcp_method, in the block below, next to
default_set.
PS-14, 2026-09-25, AND THE CLOCK IS BUILT: on the owner's instruction
("I want you to create that back ground clock") a background clock
runs a self-scan of 127.0.0.1 every poll_interval seconds and stores
it in port_scan_results like any other scan, so the port record keeps
moving when nobody asks. It costs 0.54 s per pass and writes 3 rows
plus 1 run row (measured on the reference host).
poll_interval: the clock's cadence, in seconds, floored in code at
60 so a value of 5 cannot ask for a permanently busy scanner. It was
read by nothing before this; it is read now, and the Settings card
and the boot log both say which setting is in charge.
enabled=false stops BOTH the clock and the call: run_port_scan
refuses, and nothing self-scans on a timer either. An empty port
answer with the switch off is the switch, NOT a quiet machine.
The clock is a self-scan of LOOPBACK only. It measures what is BOUND
on this host, which is deliberately not the same question as what is
reachable from another machine; every row it writes says origin=self
and carries that caveat.
Persistence on THIS host: systemd units (system and user), cron,
init.d and shell startup files. Section 7 of toolaudit.md.
enabled=false means REFUSE. This sensor is drawn on demand, not on a
clock, so the switch cannot stop a loop -- it stops the ANSWER.
query_autoruns then reads nothing and returns off_by_config=true with
count 0 and a sentence saying an empty list is not a clean machine.
The readiness page shows it as OFF rather than as running. An absent
key means ON, as it does for every other sensor here.
poll_interval is the CACHE lifetime on this sensor (seconds). It is
the one thing the key can honestly mean with no poll loop: an answer
up to this old may be returned, marked cached=true with its age. Pass
refresh=true for a live read.
L3, 2026-09-22. The integrity of THIS host, read directly, not over
SSH. linux_monitor above and below is the REMOTE one and is left
alone. This sensor needs no privilege for the half it does, and it
reports the half it cannot: /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d are
root-only, so for those only name, mode, owner, size and mtime are
watched.
poll_interval: tier A, the file and directory watch. Measured at
about a second for the whole set on the reference host.
sweep_interval_seconds: tier B, the setuid/setgid/capability sweep.
It has to walk the filesystem and MEASURED 30 to 40 seconds over
936,143 files there, which is why it is hourly and why it runs on
its own thread rather than on the poll loop. A floor of 30s is
enforced in code: a value below it asks for a permanently busy
disk, not a faster sensor.
dpkg_interval_seconds: tier C, `dpkg -V`. MEASURED 209s for a full
run over 2755 packages on the reference host, on its own thread,
default three hours. A floor of 300s is enforced in code. The
owner's instruction was 'expensive, hourly at most'; three hours
is slower than that on purpose, and the reason is that the thing
this detects -- a file a package shipped being replaced -- is not
a race with a three-hour window.
dpkg_exclude_boot: /boot is EXCLUDED BY DEFAULT. Kernel images and
System.map files legitimately churn, they are mode 600 root and so
unreadable on an ordinary run anyway, and they produced 18 of the
55 measured output lines. Set it to false on a host where /boot is
readable and stable and the check is worth having.
NOTE ON WHAT dpkg -V CANNOT DO. It compares file CONTENTS against
the md5sums dpkg recorded at unpack time. It does not check
signatures, it does not know about files no package shipped, and
on a host with one malformed control file it ABORTS with exit 2
having verified only the packages sorting before the bad one. This
sensor works around that by naming the packages it can verify and
reporting the refused ones as a coverage finding -- measured on
this host as 1 package of 2756.
T6, 2026-09-22. THE KERNEL CAMERA, read side. ebpf/ebpf_monitor.py
runs as ROOT, attaches sched_process_exec and sys_enter_connect, and
writes a file of its own; this block configures the app that READS
that file. It is the only sensor in this app that sees an execution
at the moment it happens, which is what makes a program that lives
five seconds inside a sixty-second poll gap visible at all.
events_db: where the camera writes. MUST MATCH the camera's own --out,
and scripts/install_ebpf_camera.sh is what keeps the two in step.
The default is the path that installer creates. If the camera is not
installed, the tool says so in words and does NOT report blind: a
camera that was never started is a stated limit of the machine, not a
fault in the app.
poll_interval: how often the app reads the file. MEASURED: a pass is
a handful of indexed SQLite reads over new rows only, so this is
cheap. It is NOT the camera's own cadence -- the camera writes
continuously and this only decides how often somebody looks.
stale_after_seconds: how old the newest event has to be before the
camera is reported as STOPPED. 900 is deliberately generous: a quiet
desktop legitimately executes nothing for minutes at a time, and a
tight window would report a working camera as dead. A stopped camera
is NOT reported blind, because the file was readable -- what stopped
is the recording, and anything that ran since is not seen LATE, it is
not seen at all. There is no later pass that picks it up.
path_allowlist: realpath prefixes that are never worth a finding. The
default covers systemd's own private tmp. MEASURED ON THIS HOST: a
boot executes systemd's executor out of
/tmp/systemd-private-<random>-<unit>-<random>/, which is not an
attack and would otherwise be a finding on every boot of the machine
the app is installed on. Add to this list rather than turning the
staging rule off: each entry subtracts one known-innocent shape, and
switching the rule off subtracts all of them at once.
watch_staging_directories / watch_dangerous_ports: the two rules.
/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /run/user and a user's cache or Downloads,
seen at execve time (LNX-3001 / LNX-3002); and connect(2) calls to
capture can see on the wire but cannot attribute to a process.
L4, 2026-09-22. THE KERNEL AUDIT FEED, read side. auditd is the
Linux kernel's own audit subsystem: it records syscalls, file
watches and account changes AT THE KERNEL LEVEL, with the identity
of whoever did it. On a host where it runs, its log is the deepest
always-listening feed this machine offers.
IT IS NOT INSTALLED ON THIS BOX, and that is the ordinary case: it
needs a package install and root, both of which only the operator
can do. So the reader is loaded UNCONDITIONALLY and reports the
absence in words, with the one command printed --
sudo apt install auditd
-- rather than returning an empty list, which a reader would take
as a clean bill of health. That distinction is the whole feature.
enabled: whether this app reads the log. The module still loads and
still reports the machine's own state when this is false: OFF and
BROKEN have to stay different sentences, and a reader switched off
on a host WITH auditd installed would otherwise read as a machine
with none.
log_path: WHERE TO READ INSTEAD OF WHAT auditd.conf SAYS. Absent
(the default, and what you want) means the reader asks auditd's own
configuration, falling back to /var/log/audit/audit.log. Set it
only to read a log from somewhere else -- a fixture during
verification, or a host that keeps the file off its usual path.
When it is set, the payload carries a warning if the audit
userspace is not installed, because then the file is NOT being
written by a running auditd and its age says nothing about now.
NO SEPARATE CADENCE KNOB. poll_interval is the ordinary sensor one
and 60 is right: a pass reads only what was APPENDED since the last
one, from a stored byte offset, so its cost is proportional to how
much auditd wrote rather than to how large the log is. On a host
where auditd is absent the pass returns before touching the disk.
WHAT IT RAISES. AUD-1001 when the audit configuration itself
changed (a rule added or removed -- nothing else in this app can
see that at all), AUD-1002 when a path under an audit watch was
touched with the identity the kernel recorded, AUD-1003 when the
KERNEL'S OWN SWITCH IS OFF (audit_enabled=0 -- the kernel records
nothing at all from that moment, so every later quiet answer is about
the switch rather than the machine) or when the kernel has DROPPED
records because its backlog overflowed, and AUD-1004 when the daemon
wrote DAEMON_END and stopped writing to the log. It reads the raw
records too, through query_audit_events, whose payload carries
`kernel_enabled` for the same reason: an empty record list under a
switched-off kernel is not a quiet machine.
Remote Linux host monitoring over SSH. Needs paramiko and key auth.
An unrecognised host key policy is refused loudly, because a wrong
value here is a silent trust decision.
How the port scanner behaves when a scan is asked for. Both keys are
read by tools/port_scanner.py; see register PS-13 option (c).
default_set: the port set used when a caller names none. 'common' is
the profiled list (fast, and blind to anything unprofiled),
'extended' adds 1-1024 (~6s a host), 'all' is 1-65535 (~5.5 min a
host and loud enough to look like an attack).
tcp_method: which TCP probe the scanner may use.
"auto"    (DEFAULT, and an absent key) raw SYN where CAP_NET_RAW or
root allows it, the connect test where it does not.
"syn"     SYN only. Without a raw socket the TCP pass refuses by
name instead of silently substituting a connect test.
"connect" the connect test only, even when a raw socket is
available.
An unreadable value is REPORTED on the scan payload
(tcp_method_problem) and falls back to "auto" so a typo does not stop
the scanner.
THE BLOCK THE CODE ACTUALLY READS. main.py's _linux_targets() does
config.get('linux_monitor') at TOP level, and its comment says it
accepts both the multi-host shape and the older single-host one; it
never looks under config.sensors. Both spellings are present in this
template so that editing either is visible rather than silently
ignored, but this top level one is the one that starts a collector.
hosts: a list of {label, host, user, port, key_path}; an entry
without host is skipped.
Linux-specific paths and backends.
firewall_backend: auto picks the layer of record; ufw when installed
and enabled in /etc/ufw/ufw.conf, then nftables, then iptables.
Data retention policies. A prune is an irreversible statement about
what mattered, so these are the operator's numbers and nothing here
guesses at a default. Note before shortening
packets_days: it also shortens the longest interval still detectable.
AI analyst settings
Read-only VPN state reader. Empty patterns means autodetect.
There is no VPN control path: interface_patterns only says what to
REPORT, it never brings an interface up or down.
Where this instance sits. Six positions: host, gateway, mirror,
inline, resolver, offline. Defaults to host. An unrecognised value is
refused loudly at boot, because a wrong value here makes every
downstream scope statement wrong. See core/sensors.py.
position 'host' cannot see traffic between other devices, or from
another device to the internet; it sees this host's own traffic plus
broadcast and multicast, and nothing else.
The cheap cadence: an ARP sweep every 15 minutes, recorded so that
absence becomes countable. Positives only; absence is derived against
the sweeps that ran. Python owns this schedule, not the model.
The expensive cadence: the device inventory fingerprint probe, every
21 days following Microsoft's published Defender cadence.
NOT a model tool at any privilege, because it ORIGINATES TRAFFIC.
Both the permanent list and exclusion_list default to not touching a
device, which is the right default for anything that sends packets at
somebody else's hardware.
Read-only DNS ingestion from a resolver you run (Pi-hole or AdGuard
Home). Nothing is sent and the resolver is never written to. This is
the only sensor that covers devices this host cannot see, because a
device that cannot resolve cannot connect.
Off by default: it needs a path to a real resolver's database.
Learns which countries and networks each program and device normally
reaches, and raises GEO-1001 or GEO-1002 when one reaches somewhere new
after learn_hours of learning. Devices need the OpenWrt router agent;
without it only this machine's programs are learned.
Read-only SNMP collection from the gateway. Off by default because it
needs a host and a community string, and probing a router nobody
pointed it at is worse than not collecting. Only set
AGENTAL_ROUTER_COMMUNITY in .env if you turn this on.
Leaves a durable line every N minutes so a run that lasts hours is
distinguishable from a process that died. 0 disables it.
T2, 2026-09-17. The Duty Watch's deterministic tick. NO MODEL, NO
TOKENS: it reads new findings on a timer and collapses them into
incidents. It is worth having with the model switched off and it must
keep working when the model is unreachable. See core/incident.py.
severity_floor: info and low findings do NOT open incidents at this
setting. That is a volume decision measured on a real machine (2,782
successful logins and 232 sudo rows in one evening), not a claim that
they do not matter. Lower it to 'low' or 'info' to see everything, and
expect that setting to be unreadable within a day on a busy host.
daily_cap: a cap HIT is recorded as a cap, never as an absence of
incidents, and the findings it skipped stay unaccounted so the next
tick sees them again.
enabled: false means NOTHING IS AGGREGATING FINDINGS. That is reported
as blind by query_sensor_health rather than as a quiet network.
T3, 2026-09-18. The action queue and its executor. A gated action the
agent wanted to take is FILED as a row here instead of running, so the
decision outlives the chat turn that reached it. See core/actions.py.
UNANSWERED NEVER BECOMES EXECUTED. There is no clock here that turns
silence into a yes. A request nobody answers retires (see expiry_days)
as NOT APPROVED AND NOT DENIED, which is a different sentence from
being refused.
enabled: false means NOTHING EXECUTES AN APPROVED REQUEST. The card
still says approved and the action behind it never happens. That is
reported as blind by query_action_requests and by sensor_health rather
than left to be discovered.
notify: the desktop bubble, a doorbell and not a control. Nothing is
decided from a bubble; the card is on the Action Queue tab. A missing
notify-send is reported, not swallowed.
T4, 2026-09-18. The agentic half: it wakes without being asked, looks
at what the ledger raised, and leaves a report a person can read. See
core/duty.py. Before this the model had exactly one door, /api/chat,
so if nobody typed the analyst did not exist that hour.
TWO TRIGGERS. An EMERGENCY (a UDP flood, high inbound AND outbound
volume) runs as soon as the condition is seen. FOUR REGULAR MOMENTS a
day, at local hours 9, 13, 17 and 21; each wakes, reports on up to two
findings from DIFFERENT tools, and goes back to sleep.
enabled: false means NOTHING IS INVESTIGATING ANYTHING. That is
reported as blind by query_agent_reports and by the Agents tab rather
than looking like a quiet network.
The budgets are HARD STOPS: a refusal examines NOTHING and is recorded
as 'budget', never as an absence of activity. The daily token ceiling
is counted from the duty_run rows themselves, because a counter in
memory would reset on every restart, which is not a limit. It is a
runaway stop rather than a ration: an ordinary day lands near 660,000
and a loop that has gone wrong hits the ceiling in hours.
Which module answers for each sensor role. Empty means 'use the
default for this platform', which is what almost every install wants.
It exists as config so the Windows monitor and its Linux twin can be
swapped without editing code. Example:
"process_monitor": "tools.process_monitor"
THE KNOWN-BAD LISTS, matched continuously against every destination this
app sees. tools/feed_matcher.py pulls them into the threat_feed table,
then checks packet destinations, DNS queries and TLS SNI names against
it as the traffic arrives -- so nobody has to think to ask.
FIVE FEEDS, AND THEY ARE NOT ALL THE SAME SHAPE.
feodo     keyed (AGENTAL_ABUSECH_KEY). Botnet C2 addresses.
urlhaus   keyed. Hosts serving malware.
threatfox KEYLESS (corrected 2026-09-27, this line said "keyed"):
its plaintext CSV export answers without a key, MEASURED
on this host. Recent IOCs with the malware family attached.
misp      KEYLESS. CIRCL's OSINT MISP feed - community-published
reports with the indicators in them.
otx       KEYED (AGENTAL_OTX_KEY). AlienVault OTX pulses.
MISP IS AN ARCHIVE, NOT A LIST, and that is why it has its own knobs.
It holds ~1,681 events, one JSON file each, at a MEASURED 2.0 MB
average. Mirroring it is not possible on any useful clock, so each
refresh reads the MANIFEST and fetches the NEWEST N EVENTS. Every
surface says so: a finding from MISP names the event, and the feed's
status carries how many events were read and how many were left.
An indicator listed only in an OLD event is therefore absent from the
table, which is a stated limit rather than a silent one.
OTX NEEDS ITS OWN KEY. MEASURED: every bulk endpoint answers HTTP 403
'Authentication required' without one. A free key from
otx.alienvault.com (Settings -> API key). With no key the feed reports
WHY in words and the rest of the matcher carries on -- a refusal is not
allowed to look like a feed that found nothing.
refresh_hours: 6 is chosen for POLITENESS as much as cost. The default
MISP window is ~30 MB and ~100 s of download per refresh; hourly would
be 750 MB a day from a free university service, which is how a project
gets blocked rather than throttled.
match_interval_seconds: matching is local SQL and is meant to be often.
The point of the whole feature is that a bad destination is noticed as
it happens rather than when somebody asks.
feeds: which lists to pull. Leave it out for all of them. A name here
that is not a feed is REPORTED rather than ignored, because a typo in
this list is a person believing a list is being pulled.
misp_max_events / otx_max_pulses: the per-feed windows, clamped in
code to 60 and 100. A config value above the ceiling is refused rather
than honoured, so a typo cannot turn a boot into a gigabyte download.
